title: BLLM: Beyond the LLM with Deep Human-Mind-AI
summary: A system that improves itself keeps every change that passes a check, so a check that makes errors lets mistakes pile up. We compute the least checking that keeps such a system sound. It is an entropy of the costs of the changes, and an endless chain of improvements stays sound at finite cost exactly when that entropy is finite. A stack of checked layers costs more than its layers would cost alone. We also compute how many guesses a proposer needs before a right one appears: human authors come close to this least number, and language models need 1.5 to 4.3 times as many. Anaxia, an engine…
